thread.title: What Can Investors Anticipate From Intel's Results? - Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC)

author: Perfect Alpha
title: What Can Investors Anticipate From Intel's Results? - Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC)
text:
Things to Watch on Thursday: Intel ( INTC ) is inverting its competitors' trends. Despite the majority of the chip companies indicating weak semiconductor demand in recent months, Intel has been facing somewhat the opposite - supply shortages paired with robust demand in semiconductors. We will listen for signs of above seasonal 1Q softness in datacenter and client compute (this includes the modem business with Apple ( AAPL )) as well as updates on expanded 14nm supply and initial 10nm ramp progress.
On the plus side, Intel has good long-term opportunities. Intel has been dominant across the PC market and it has significant exposure to different high-growth semiconductor markets, including automotive, edge-/end-point devices, NAND storage, AI and machine learning and memory chips. Its diversified business model gives itself a significant competitive edge relative to its peers, allowing them to be flexible on distributing resources and quickly adapting to updated market trends.
On the con side, Intel has some pressing issues. Intel's core PC market has been stagnant over the past quarters. It's struggling with node transitions and has likely lost its manufacturing lead (once core to its competitive advantage). The industry has become more and more competitive, with the likes of AMD ( AMD ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) rolling out aggressive products and concepts, and the industry-wide shift from general-purpose chips toward specialized chips have enabled new yet significant competitors, such as Google ( GOOG ) ( GOOGL ), Facebook ( FB ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Amazon ( AMZN ).
Intel still needs a CEO. Intel remains in search of a permanent CEO, but it's unlikely that they will have an answer by Thursday. Interim CEO (and current CFO) Bob Swan has been meeting expectations and has a satisfactory performance, but he already has distanced himself from taking on the role permanently. The new CEO will be tasked with the crucial decision of Intel's future positioning within the semiconductor market given that its significant competitive edge in manufacturing is nonexistent anymore. Intel still owns an enormous ecosystem, a massive war chest, and amazing engineering talent. However, the direction and focus of the company has become less clear. The progression of its existing competitors (AMD and Nvidia) and the emergence of new competitors (Google, Apple, Amazon, etc.) imply that Intel will need to form a clear growth strategy in order to maintain its market dominance.
Market Outlook We have come up with several macro downside risks that might be mentioned on Thursday. These are general industry-wide headwinds to the semiconductor industry, and we expect them to be a recurring risk for Intel and its main competitors in the upcoming year.
Key downside risks include China's economic slowdown, slower smartphone sales globally, softer demand for autos R&D, the US government shutdown hurting high-end consumer spending (including PC-related products) and the ongoing trade war.

However, due to the industry-wide risks as outlined above, we expect a more negative year ahead compared to previous years. Therefore, the growth associated with the past few years is unlikely to replicate itself in 2019. Nonetheless, Intel remains a buy in our opinion as it's still well positioned in its long-term growth opportunities and is much more diversified than its competitors.
